question: I run a goods-only trading business in Pune, Maharashtra and sell only within Maharashtra. My total turnover in the last financial year was Rs 42,00,000. Do I have to register for GST? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 10/2019-CT (exemption for exclusive suppliers of goods up to Rs 40 lakh) - https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-10-central-tax-english-2019.pdf

question: I sell only goods, all within Telangana, from Hyderabad. My turnover last financial year was Rs 30,00,000. Is GST registration mandatory for me? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 10/2019-CT excludes intra-State suppliers in Telangana (and 9 other States/UTs) from the Rs 40 lakh limit, so the Rs 20 lakh goods limit applies - https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-10-central-tax-english-2019.pdf ; CBIC 'GST - An Update' (1 Apr 2019) lists the 10 States at Rs 20 lakh - https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/01042019_GST-An-Update.pdf

question: I run a goods-only shop in Imphal, Manipur and sell only within Manipur. My turnover last financial year was Rs 15,00,000. Do I need to register for GST? Answer yes or no.
source: Manipur is one of the ten States with a Rs 20 lakh goods threshold (not Rs 10 lakh) - CBIC 'GST - An Update' https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/01042019_GST-An-Update.pdf ; Notification 10/2019-CT https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-10-central-tax-english-2019.pdf

question: I sell only goods, all within Assam, from Guwahati. My turnover last financial year was Rs 30,00,000. Is GST registration mandatory? Answer yes or no.
source: Assam is not among the ten States excluded by Notification 10/2019-CT, so the general Rs 40 lakh goods threshold applies - https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-10-central-tax-english-2019.pdf ; CBIC 'GST - An Update' https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/01042019_GST-An-Update.pdf

question: I am a consultant providing only services from Dehradun, Uttarakhand, to clients within Uttarakhand. My turnover last financial year was Rs 15,00,000. Must I register for GST? Answer yes or no.
source: Services threshold is Rs 20 lakh; Rs 10 lakh applies only in Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura - CBIC 'GST - An Update' (1 Apr 2019) https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/01042019_GST-An-Update.pdf

question: I am a goods trader in Delhi with a turnover of Rs 15,00,000 last financial year. I sometimes ship goods to customers in Punjab (inter-State). Do I have to register for GST? Answer yes or no.
source: CGST Act s.24(i): inter-State taxable supply requires registration irrespective of turnover; the only turnover-based inter-State relief is for services (Notification 10/2017-IT) and notified handicrafts (Notification 3/2018-IT) - https://taxguru.in/?p=1029615 ; https://cbic-gst.gov.in/pdf/01042019_GST-An-Update.pdf

question: I am a garment trader in Bengaluru, Karnataka selling only goods within Karnataka, with a turnover of Rs 1,20,00,000 last financial year. Can I opt for the GST composition scheme? Answer yes or no.
source: Composition turnover limit Rs 1.5 crore (Rs 75 lakh in 8 listed States), Notification 14/2019-CT - https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-14-central-tax-english-2019.pdf ; CGST Act s.10(2) - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1752317902-section-10.pdf

question: I am a garment trader in Gangtok, Sikkim, selling only goods within Sikkim, with a turnover of Rs 90,00,000 last financial year. Can I opt for the GST composition scheme? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 14/2019-CT limits composition to Rs 75 lakh for Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura and Uttarakhand - https://www.gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-14-central-tax-english-2019.pdf

question: My company's aggregate turnover in the previous financial year was Rs 5.2 crore. Is e-invoicing mandatory for us under GST from 2026? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 10/2023-CT: e-invoicing applies where aggregate turnover exceeds Rs 5 crore in any preceding FY from 2017-18, effective 1 Aug 2023 - https://www.ey.com/en_in/technical/alerts-hub/2023/05/cbic-lowers-turnover-threshold-for-e-invoicing-to-inr5-crores-with-effect-from-1-august-2023

question: My company's aggregate turnover in the previous financial year was exactly Rs 5,00,00,000 (Rs 5 crore). Is e-invoicing mandatory for us under GST in 2026? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 10/2023-CT applies only where turnover EXCEEDS Rs 5 crore - https://www.ey.com/en_in/technical/alerts-hub/2023/05/cbic-lowers-turnover-threshold-for-e-invoicing-to-inr5-crores-with-effect-from-1-august-2023

question: My business had a turnover of Rs 8 crore last financial year. How many digits of HSN code must I show on my B2B tax invoices (from 1 April 2021 onwards)? Give a number.
source: Notification 78/2020-CT as explained in the PIB release of 2021: 6-digit HSN above Rs 5 crore, 4-digit up to Rs 5 crore, from 1 Apr 2021 - https://pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1708713

question: What was the GST rate (CGST+SGST/IGST combined, excluding cess) on Portland cement, HSN 252329, on 21 September 2025? Give a percentage.
source: Cement was 28% until the 56th Council changes took effect on 22 Sep 2025 - PIB https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202594628401.pdf (cement 28% to 18%)

question: What is the GST rate (combined, excluding cess) on Portland cement, HSN 252329, on 22 September 2025? Give a percentage.
source: Notification 9/2025-CT(Rate), Schedule II (9% CGST) via CBIC ready reckoner - https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf ; PIB https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202594628401.pdf

question: What is the GST rate on toilet soap in bars (HSN 340111) on 10 January 2026? Give a percentage.
source: Notification 9/2025-CT(Rate), Schedule I S.No.251 (2.5% CGST, toilet soap in bars) - CBIC ready reckoner https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf

question: What is the GST rate on rice that is sold pre-packaged and labelled (HSN 100630) on 1 March 2026? Give a percentage.
source: Notification 9/2025-CT(Rate), Schedule I S.No.48: rice only when pre-packaged and labelled, 2.5% CGST - CBIC ready reckoner https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf

question: What is the GST rate on vegetables preserved otherwise than by vinegar and not frozen (HSN 200599, e.g. canned mixed vegetables) on 1 February 2026? Give a percentage.
source: Notification 9/2025-CT(Rate), Schedule I S.No.129 (heading 2005), 2.5% CGST - CBIC ready reckoner https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf

question: What is the GST rate (excluding any cess) on a petrol SUV with a 2,500 cc engine and length over 4 metres, HSN 870323, on 1 February 2026? Give a percentage.
source: Notification 9/2025-CT(Rate), Schedule III S.No.5 (heading 8703 other cars, 20% CGST = 40%); compensation cess on motor vehicles reduced to nil - CBIC ready reckoner https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf ; PIB https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202594628401.pdf

question: What is the GST rate on filter cigarettes (HSN 240220) on 1 March 2026? Give a percentage for GST only, not cess or excise.
source: From 1 Feb 2026 GST on cigarettes is 40% and compensation cess is nil (Notification 19/2025-CT(Rate); Compensation Cess (Rate) 03/2025) - https://www.livelaw.in/amp/tax-cases/new-rsp-based-valuation-mechanism-40-gst-rate-on-pan-masala-cigarettes-cigars-tobacco-products-from-february-01-516688

question: A Mumbai (Maharashtra) manufacturer sells Portland cement (HSN 252329) worth Rs 1,00,000 to a buyer in Pune (Maharashtra) on 15 January 2026. How much CGST is charged? Give rupees.
source: Cement is 18% from 22 Sep 2025 (Notification 9/2025-CT(Rate), Sch II); intra-State supply splits equally into CGST 9% and SGST 9% (CGST Act s.9, SGST Act) - https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf ; https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202594628401.pdf

question: A Mumbai (Maharashtra) manufacturer sells Portland cement (HSN 252329) worth Rs 1,00,000 to a buyer in Bengaluru (Karnataka) on 15 January 2026. How much IGST is charged? Give rupees.
source: Inter-State supply attracts IGST at the full 18% (IGST Act s.5; Notification 9/2025-IT(Rate)) - https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf ; https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202594628401.pdf

question: A Delhi IT reseller invoices 5 laptops (HSN 8471) at Rs 50,000 each to a company in Haryana on 10 February 2026, with a Rs 10,000 trade discount shown on the invoice itself. How much IGST is payable on the invoice? Give rupees.
source: Value excludes a discount recorded on the invoice (CGST Act s.15(3)(a)) so taxable value is Rs 2,40,000; laptops 18% (Sch II S.No.456) - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1756722144-section-15.pdf ; https://a2ztaxcorp.net/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/CBIC-GST-Ready-Reckoner-indicating-updated-Central-Goods-and-Services-Tax-CGST-rates-on-goods.pdf

question: A dealer in Nashik, Maharashtra sells a 150 cc motorcycle (HSN 871120) for Rs 1,00,000 (before tax) to a customer in Nashik on 1 June 2025. What is the total GST including any compensation cess? Give rupees.
source: Before 22 Sep 2025 motorcycles up to 350 cc were 28% GST; compensation cess (3%) applied only above 350 cc, nil at or below - Compensation Cess (Rate) Notification 1/2017 S.No.53 https://taxindiaonline.com/RC2/pdfnoti/gst/cess_rate/2017/cess_rate_01.pdf ; PIB https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/sep/doc202594628401.pdf (28% to 18%)

question: A GST-registered manufacturing company in Mumbai, Maharashtra pays an individual advocate in Mumbai Rs 1,00,000 for legal advice (SAC 998212) on 20 January 2026. Under reverse charge, how much GST must the company itself pay to the government? Give rupees.
source: Notification 13/2017-CT(Rate) Sl.2: services by an advocate to a business entity are taxed on reverse charge, recipient pays - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_8_0.pdf ; legal services SAC 9982 at 18% - https://cleartax.in/s/legal-services-gst-rates-sac-code-9982

question: A GST-registered factory in Pune, Maharashtra pays a goods transport agency (GTA) Rs 50,000 freight for road transport of goods on 20 January 2026. The GTA charges no GST on the invoice because it has not opted for the 18% (with ITC) rate. At the 5% rate, how much GST must the factory pay under reverse charge? Give rupees.
source: Notification 13/2017-CT(Rate) Sl.1: GTA road goods transport, recipient pays under reverse charge - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_8_0.pdf ; GTA 5% without ITC (18% with ITC option from 22 Sep 2025) - https://lakshmisri.com/newsroom/news-briefings/impact-of-gst-rate-changes-on-the-logistic-sector

question: Our trading company bought a passenger car (HSN 8703, seating 5) for the managing director's use. The supplier invoice (GST Rs 1,20,000) appears in both our purchase register and GSTR-2B. The car is not used for resale, passenger transport or driving training. How much input tax credit can we claim on it? Give rupees.
source: CGST Act s.17(5)(a): ITC blocked on motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating capacity of 13 or fewer, except further supply, passenger transport or driving training - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1753685259-section-17.pdf

question: A transport company bought a new goods carrier truck (HSN 8704) for carrying goods. The supplier invoice (GST Rs 2,80,000) appears in both our purchase register and GSTR-2B. How much input tax credit can we claim on it? Give rupees.
source: CGST Act s.17(5)(a) blocks only vehicles for transport of persons (13 seats or fewer); goods vehicles are outside the block - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1753685259-section-17.pdf

question: Our software company paid a restaurant caterer (SAC 996331) for a staff party. The invoice (GST Rs 9,000) is in both our books and GSTR-2B. We do not sell food, and no law obliges us to provide it. How much input tax credit can we claim? Give rupees.
source: CGST Act s.17(5)(b)(i): ITC blocked on food and beverages and outdoor catering unless used for outward supply of the same category or obligatory under law - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1753685259-section-17.pdf

question: I am a regular monthly filer in Gujarat with turnover above Rs 5 crore. What is the due date for the GSTR-3B for October 2026? Give a date.
source: CGST Rules r.61(1)(i): monthly GSTR-3B by the 20th of the following month - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule61_v1.00.html

question: I am a QRMP (quarterly) filer in Maharashtra. What is the due date for the quarterly GSTR-1 for April-June 2026? Give a date.
source: Notification 83/2020-CT: quarterly GSTR-1 by the 13th of the month after the quarter - https://gstgyaan.com/section-37-furnishing-details-of-outward-supplies-in-gstr-1 ; r.59 - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule59_v1.00.html

question: I am a QRMP (quarterly) filer with my principal place of business in Maharashtra. What is the due date for the GSTR-3B for April-June 2026? Give a date.
source: CGST Rules r.61(1)(ii) Table Sl.1: Maharashtra and listed States - 22nd day of the month after the quarter - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule61_v1.00.html

question: I am a QRMP (quarterly) filer with my principal place of business in Delhi. What is the due date for the GSTR-3B for April-June 2026? Give a date.
source: CGST Rules r.61(1)(ii) Table Sl.2: Delhi and listed States/UTs - 24th day of the month after the quarter - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule61_v1.00.html

question: I am a QRMP (quarterly) filer with my principal place of business in Kerala. What is the due date for the GSTR-3B for April-June 2026? Give a date.
source: CGST Rules r.61(1)(ii) Table Sl.1: Kerala is in the 22nd-day group - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule61_v1.00.html

question: I am a QRMP (quarterly) filer. By what date can I upload invoices for April 2026 (the first month of the quarter) using the Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF)? Give a date.
source: CGST Rules r.59(2): IFF for the first and second months of a quarter, from the 1st to the 13th of the following month - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule59_v1.00.html ; https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/notfctn-82-central-tax-english-2020.pdf

question: I am a QRMP (quarterly) filer. Can I use the Invoice Furnishing Facility (IFF) for June 2026, the third month of the quarter? Answer yes or no.
source: CGST Rules r.59(2): IFF is available only for the first and second months of a quarter - https://taxinformation.cbic.gov.in/content/html/tax_repository/gst/rules/cgst_rules/active/chapter8/rule59_v1.00.html

question: In October 2026 my Maharashtra firm sold goods to an unregistered individual in Karnataka for Rs 1,50,000 plus 18% IGST (Rs 27,000). Must this invoice be reported invoice-by-invoice in GSTR-1 Table 5 (B2C Large) rather than being clubbed into the B2C-others table? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 12/2024-CT (10 Jul 2024) lowered the invoice-wise reporting threshold for inter-State supplies to unregistered persons from Rs 2.5 lakh to Rs 1 lakh - https://www.taxscan.in/gstn-issues-advisory-on-reporting-supplies-to-unregistered-dealers-in-gstr-1-gstr-5/433979

question: I run a trading business (not a profession) and my FY 2025-26 turnover was Rs 2.8 crore, with 97% of receipts through bank transfers/UPI and only 3% in cash. Can I use presumptive taxation under section 44AD? Answer yes or no.
source: Income-tax Act s.44AD: limit Rs 3 crore if cash receipts do not exceed 5% of total, else Rs 2 crore - https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/itr-4

question: I run a trading business and my FY 2025-26 turnover was Rs 2.5 crore, but 20% of my receipts were in cash. Can I use presumptive taxation under section 44AD? Answer yes or no.
source: Income-tax Act s.44AD: the Rs 3 crore limit needs cash receipts of 5% or less; otherwise the limit is Rs 2 crore - https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/itr-4

question: I am a practising doctor (individual) with FY 2025-26 gross receipts of Rs 60 lakh, 98% received digitally. Can I use presumptive taxation under section 44ADA? Answer yes or no.
source: Income-tax Act s.44ADA: limit Rs 75 lakh if cash receipts do not exceed 5%, else Rs 50 lakh - https://www.incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/help/all-topics/e-filing-services/itr-4

question: I am a salaried employee with gross salary of Rs 18,00,000 in FY 2025-26 and no other income or deductions. Under the new tax regime (with the Rs 75,000 standard deduction), what is my total tax including 4% cess? Give rupees.
source: New-regime slabs for FY 2025-26 (nil to 4L, 5%, 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 30%), standard deduction Rs 75,000, cess 4% - https://cleartax.in/s/hi/income-tax-slabs ; https://www.business-standard.com/amp/finance/personal-finance/new-rules-from-april-1-zero-tax-on-income-up-to-rs-12l-see-all-changes-125040200823_1.html

question: I am a salaried employee with gross salary of Rs 12,80,000 in FY 2025-26 and no other income or deductions. Under the new tax regime (Rs 75,000 standard deduction), what is my total tax including 4% cess? Give rupees.
source: Section 87A rebate with marginal relief: tax above Rs 12 lakh income is capped at the excess over Rs 12 lakh (here taxable Rs 12,05,000 so tax Rs 5,000 + 4% cess) - https://www.allindiaitr.com/marginal-relief-income-above-12-lakh

question: I am a chartered engineer in Pune providing only consulting services to clients in Maharashtra. My turnover last financial year was Rs 30,00,000. If I opt for the GST composition scheme, what is the maximum preceding-year turnover allowed for my scheme, in rupees? Answer with a number.
source: Notification 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), 7 Mar 2019, w.e.f. 1 Apr 2019 - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_2024-05-17t161230.215.pdf (entry: first supplies up to Rs 50 lakh; condition 1(i): preceding-FY turnover Rs 50 lakh or below); CGST Act s.10(1) second proviso and s.10(2A) - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1752317902-section-10.pdf (s.10(1) closed to a pure service provider beyond the 10%/Rs 5 lakh allowance)

question: I am a consultant in Pune providing only services within Maharashtra, turnover Rs 30,00,000 last financial year. Under the composition scheme for service providers, what total GST rate (CGST plus SGST) do I pay on my turnover? Answer with a percentage.
source: Notification 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), 7 Mar 2019, w.e.f. 1 Apr 2019 - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_2024-05-17t161230.215.pdf (column 2: central tax 3%; the State notification under the SGST Act levies the matching 3%)

question: I run an interior design consultancy in Bengaluru, Karnataka, services only, all clients within Karnataka. Turnover last financial year was Rs 55,00,000. Can I opt for the GST composition scheme? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), 7 Mar 2019, w.e.f. 1 Apr 2019 - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_2024-05-17t161230.215.pdf (condition 1(i): preceding-FY turnover Rs 50 lakh or below); CGST Act s.10(1) second proviso and s.10(2A) - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1752317902-section-10.pdf (the Rs 1.5 crore limit is for s.10(1), which a pure service provider cannot use)

question: I am a software consultant in Pune with Rs 30,00,000 turnover last financial year, services only. Some of my clients are in Karnataka and Gujarat. Can I opt for the 6% composition scheme for service providers? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), 7 Mar 2019, w.e.f. 1 Apr 2019 - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_2024-05-17t161230.215.pdf (condition 1(iv): not engaged in any inter-State outward supply); CGST Act s.10(2A)(b)

question: I offer home-cleaning services in Mumbai, all booked through an app that collects TCS under section 52. Turnover last financial year was Rs 25,00,000, services only, all within Maharashtra. Can I opt for the GST composition scheme? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), 7 Mar 2019, w.e.f. 1 Apr 2019 - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_2024-05-17t161230.215.pdf (condition 1(vi): no supply through an e-commerce operator who collects TCS under s.52); CGST Act s.10(2A)(c)

question: I run a shop in Nagpur, Maharashtra. Last financial year I sold Rs 20,00,000 of goods, including pan masala (HSN 2106 90 20), and earned Rs 20,00,000 from repair services, all within Maharashtra. Can I opt for the 6% composition scheme? Answer yes or no.
source: Notification 2/2019-Central Tax (Rate), 7 Mar 2019, w.e.f. 1 Apr 2019 - https://gstcouncil.gov.in/sites/default/files/2024-05/download_2024-05-17t161230.215.pdf (condition 1(vii) and Annexure S.No.2: pan masala 2106 90 20 is excluded); services above the s.10(1) allowance put this person under s.10(2A) - CGST Act s.10(1) second proviso and s.10(2A) - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1752317902-section-10.pdf

question: I trade goods in Pune, all within Maharashtra: Rs 40,00,000 of goods and Rs 4,50,000 of installation services last financial year. Which composition route applies to me: the regular scheme under section 10(1) or the services scheme under section 10(2A)? Answer s10_1 or s10_2A.
source: CGST Act s.10(1) second proviso and s.10(2A) - https://www.cggst.com/uploads/document/1752317902-section-10.pdf (second proviso: services up to the higher of 10% of turnover or Rs 5 lakh are allowed under s.10(1); here Rs 4.5 lakh is within Rs 5 lakh, so s.10(2A), which is only for persons not eligible under s.10(1), does not apply)
